title: Rovinj with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules and Costs
metaDescription: Rovinj with a dog in 2027: official dog beaches, old town and restaurant rules, ferry and park rules, hotel dog fees, summer heat, vets and EU pet passport.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Rovinj (Plaža za Pse)

Rovinj's tourist board marks specific spots where dogs may swim. The official list covers Borik (from the northern wall of the hospital), the quarry in the Zlatni rt forest park, Škaraba, Cuvi (towards Villas Rubin), the beach across from Luigi Monti street at Bolničko naselje, Kaštelan cove (towards Amarin), Veštar cove (past the Mon Paradis campsite) and Cisterna cove. Lone Bay also has a section reserved for dogs.

Most of these are rocky or gravel coves, not sand. Bring dog shoes for sensitive paws and a shade umbrella, because several coves have little natural shade.

### Are dogs allowed on other beaches in Rovinj?

No. Dogs are generally not permitted on the main public swimming beaches, and the rule is to use the signposted dog sections only. At Borik, pets are banned on the beach below the car park. The dog section sits at the far southern end, next to the orthopaedic hospital boundary. Resort beaches such as Amarin allow dogs only in designated parts.

Don't trust blog posts that say Rovinj lets dogs go anywhere. The town is dog-friendly because it has many marked dog coves and a large forest park, not because beaches are open to dogs. Fines for ignoring beach signs are a poor way to start a holiday.

## Dogs in Rovinj Old Town and Restaurants

The old town is compact and walkable on a leash, and the harbour promenade and Zlatni rt (Punta Corrente) park are both leash-friendly. The stone streets get very hot at midday in July and August. Walk before 09:00 or after 19:00 to protect paws.

Outdoor restaurant terraces commonly accept dogs, and it is polite to ask first. Indoor dining is at the owner's discretion, and many places say no. Keep the dog leashed, and carry water and a bowl, since few venues provide one.

### Zlatni rt (Punta Corrente) Forest Park

The park covers roughly 300 acres of pine and holm oak woodland. It has shaded trails, and several of the dog coves sit inside or beside it. It is the best daily walk for a dog in Rovinj, and it stays cooler than the town in summer.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans

**National parks.** Rules differ by park. Krka allows leashed dogs, but not on Visovac island, and a muzzle is required on its shuttle buses and boats. Check the park's own rules before booking tickets for Brijuni (a short trip from Fažana, near Pula) or Plitvice.

**Ferries.** Jadrolinija allows dogs on most routes, usually on open deck or in the car, on a leash and often with a muzzle. Rules are stricter on catamarans, and a carrier is sometimes required. Some routes charge a pet ticket and others do not, so confirm when booking. Rovinj also has a seasonal fast catamaran to Venice. Confirm the pet policy with the operator before buying tickets.

Croatia's law requires a leash everywhere in public. Restricted breeds, including some bull terrier types, must wear a muzzle, and bull terrier types not registered with the FCI cannot enter.

## What Accommodation Charges for a Dog

Pet-friendly apartments and hotels in Istria typically add a dog fee. Expect roughly €10 to €20 per night for a dog, or a flat cleaning fee of about €30 to €60 per stay. Some private apartments accept dogs free of charge. Many hosts limit the number of dogs to one or two, and some exclude larger breeds. Always confirm in writing before paying a deposit. Campsites commonly charge a separate daily dog fee in summer, and they often keep dogs off the campsite's beach.

Stay near Zlatni rt or Cuvi for the shortest walk to a dog cove. A car is not needed if you stay within walking distance of Lone Bay.

## Summer Heat and the Best Months

July and August bring hot days, hot pavement and warm sea. Heat stress is the main risk for dogs in Istria. Never leave a dog in a parked car, and avoid walks between 11:00 and 17:00.

- **May to June:** Best balance of warm water, long days and fewer restrictions. Beaches are quiet.
- **Late September:** Sea still warm, cooler air, and lower accommodation prices.
- **April and October:** Good for hiking in Zlatni rt, but cool for swimming.
- **July and August:** Possible, but plan around early mornings and evenings, and book accommodation with air conditioning.

## Vet Basics

Carry the vet's contact details and your dog's vaccination record. The nearest 24-hour emergency vet is about 38 km from Rovinj, so plan the drive for any urgent case. Rovinj has local clinics for routine care. Pharmacies for animals are in town. Tick prevention is worth using in the wooded areas of Zlatni rt, and many vets also advise protection against sandflies and mosquitoes in summer.

## EU Pet Passport and Entry Rules for Driving In

For dogs travelling within the EU, three things are required:

1. **Microchip.** It must be ISO 11784/11785 compliant (15 digits) and implanted before the rabies vaccination.
2. **Rabies vaccination.** Given at least 21 days before travel for a first vaccination, and the dog must be at least 12 weeks old. A booster inside the validity period needs no new waiting period.
3. **EU pet passport.** Issued by an authorised vet to owners resident in the EU. A new EU regulation (2026/131) replaced the old rules in April 2026, and existing passports remain valid.

Travellers from outside the EU, for example from the UK, generally need an Animal Health Certificate instead of an EU passport. Croatia's border information also lists a muzzle and leash for dogs in transit. Tapeworm treatment is required only for entry into Finland, Ireland, Malta, Norway and Northern Ireland, so it matters if the route passes through those countries. Pet passports cost about €10 plus VAT at a Croatian vet.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Rovinj?

**Rovinj is very dog-friendly, about 8 out of 10.** It has around eight marked dog coves, a large forest park, and a walkable old town where leashed dogs are accepted. The weak points are rocky beaches with little shade, strict limits on dogs at the main beaches, hot summer pavement and indoor restaurants that often refuse dogs. A dog owner who plans around the dog sections and visits in May, June or September will find Rovinj one of the easiest bases on the Istrian coast.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on beaches in Rovinj?
faq.answer: Only in the marked dog sections, such as Lone Bay, Cuvi, Škaraba, Borik (southern end), Kaštelan, Veštar and Cisterna. Dogs are generally not allowed on the main public swimming beaches. Look for the signs, which are usually in Croatian and Italian.

faq.question: Can I take my dog into Rovinj old town and restaurants?
faq.answer: Leashed dogs can walk the old town and harbour promenade. Restaurant terraces commonly accept dogs, but indoor seating is up to each owner, so ask first.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to travel to Croatia by car?
faq.answer: A readable ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination (given at least 21 days before travel for a first dose) and an EU pet passport. Non-EU travellers generally need an Animal Health Certificate. Carry the documents in the car, because they may be checked at the border.

faq.question: How much do hotels and apartments charge for a dog in Rovinj?
faq.answer: A typical dog fee is about €10 to €20 per night, or a flat cleaning fee of roughly €30 to €60 per stay. Some private apartments charge nothing. Confirm the fee and any size limit before booking.

faq.question: What is the best month to visit Rovinj with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and late September are best, with warm water, cooler air and quieter coves. July and August are hot, and pavement can burn paws, so walks need to be early or late.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on ferries and catamarans in Croatia?
faq.answer: Jadrolinija accepts dogs on most routes, usually on a leash and often with a muzzle, and large dogs usually stay on deck. Catamaran rules are stricter, so check the operator's policy before booking.

quickAnswer: Rovinj is one of the easiest dog destinations in Istria. The town has about eight marked dog beach sections, including Lone, Cuvi, Škaraba and Borik. Leashed dogs can walk the old town and the Zlatni rt forest park. Dogs need a microchip, a rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. Visit in May, June or late September.
